resources.string: Determines the sensitivity for detecting stars in a captured image. Increase to detect more stars. Note: increasing the value too much can slow down the solver and/or result in more false stars detected.
Increase the camera\'s zoom for avoiding obstructions at the edges of the image. Note: zooming in reduces the usable image for star detection.
Increase the exposure to gather more light in a captured image. Slower exposures (higher number) increase star detection at the cost of slower updates.
Combine data from multiple frames into a single image prior to star detection. This slows down the effective exposure rate for the camera.
Increase the brightness of the image. Unlike gain, the brightness value is applied after the image is captured by the sensor.

Increase the camera\'s brightness / light sensitivity. By default the ISO value is set to the highest analog value supported by the camera. Any increase beyond this will also increase noise artifacts.
Increase the camera sensor\'s light sensitivity.
Change the focus position of the camera.
Enable software noise reduction in the camera\'s image processor.
Enable hot pixel removal in the camera\'s image processor.
Half-Flux Radius is used to measure the size, sharpness, and focus of detected stars. Lower values indicate a better focus of the camera when it\'s pointed at the sky.

Internal Camera
Use the device\'s native camera for imaging the sky.

External Camera
Use a camera plugged into the device\'s USB port.

Demo Camera
Cycles through canned images for demo purposes.
Processed mode (recommended) uses the camera\'s own algorithms to pre-process the image. Raw mode relies on the engine to do the processing. Raw is only available on select phone models.
Based on this setting the image will be reduced in size prior to running the plate-solving algorithms.
The engine\'s guidance display can show Alt-Az offsets (distance to target) or equatorial RA/Dec offsets.
Swaps the left and right positions of on-screen Sky Map overlays and controls (clock, stats, position, centering, zoom, and guidance).

Olive Finder runs control servers for external connections:
- Meade LX200 protocol on port 4030
- ASCOM Alpaca protocol on port 11111
- ASCOM Alpaca discovery server

SkySafari Integration

Configuring SkySafari 7/8 Plus or Pro (Alpaca)
Menu > Settings > Telescope section - Presets
Add Preset > ASCOM Alpaca
Manual Configuration:
- IP Address - 127.0.0.1 if using the same phone as Olive Finder, otherwise the IP address displayed in Olive Finder\'s screen
- Port - 11111
Check IP and Port for Devices
Next
- Preset Name: Olive
- Set Time & Location: leave this checked only if Olive is on a separate device
- Readout Rate: 10 per second (Important: swipe back instead of pressing the X)
Save Preset
Select the new preset > Use This Preset

Configuring SkySafari 7/8 Plus or Pro (LX200)
Menu > Settings > Telescope section - Presets
Add Preset > Other Connection > Meade LX200 Classic, Next > Alt-Az. GoTo (Recommended), Next
Connect via WiFi
- IP Address - localhost if using the same phone as Olive Finder, otherwise the IP address displayed in Olive Finder\'s screen
- Port - 4030
Check Connection
Next
- Preset Name: Olive
- Set Time & Location: leave this checked only if Olive is on a separate device
- Readout Rate: 10 per second (Important: swipe back instead of pressing the X)
Save Preset
Select the new preset > Use This Preset

Configuring SkySafari 6 Plus or Pro (LX200)
Settings > Telescope section - Setup
- Scope Type -- Meade LX200 Classic
- Mount Type -- Alt-Az. GoTo (Recommended)
- Connect via WiFi
- IP Address - localhost if using the same phone as Olive Finder, otherwise the IP address displayed in Olive Finder\'s screen
- Port - 4030
- Set Time & Location: leave this checked only if Olive is on a separate device
- Readout Rate -- 10 per second (Important: swipe back instead of pressing the X)
Press X

SkySafari Usage
Scope > Connect
Select an Object
- GoTo -> Olive will show guidance to the object
- Stop -> Stop the current GoTo target
- Align -> Center object in eyepiece, tap Align to update Olive\'s alignment*

Stellarium Integration

Configuring Stellarium+ (LX200)
Menu > Observing Tools > Telescope Control (toggle on)
Type - Network
Host - localhost if using the same phone as Olive Finder, otherwise the IP address displayed in Olive Finder\'s screen
Toggle Link to on
Time and Location sync - Turn off if using Olive on the same device

Stellarium Usage
Menu > Observing Tools > Telescope Control (toggle on)
Toggle Link to on
Select an Object
- GoTo -> Olive will show guidance to the object
- Sync -> Center object in eyepiece, tap Sync to update Olive\'s alignment*

* Olive uses a single alignment point to determine the offset of the camera\'s view to the telescope\'s view. Alignment only needs to be done once each time the camera is mounted on a telescope.
